solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ancient stone vessel found in protective wrapping

indicators.note: something found in a wrapping is enclosed by it, so the ship goes inside

parts.note: foil is a thin metal sheet wrapped round food to protect it
SS is steamship, a common abbreviation for a vessel

explanation.surface: An archaeologist unwraps an old stone pot that was carefully packed for transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is a remnant of ancient life preserved in rock, literally an ancient stone.

clue.text: Noisy oriental entertainment

parts.note: F is forte, the musical marking for loud
oriental means from the East

explanation.surface: A loud show put on in an Eastern style.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a lavish meal given to entertain guests, so it is a form of hospitality.

clue.text: Weapon not used at the front?

definitions.text: Weapon not used at the front?

parts.words: Weapon not used at the front?
parts.note: a pistol is worn at the side rather than fired at the battle front, and it is not carried in front of the body

explanation.surface: A question about which weapon stays out of frontline combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a pistol or sword carried at the hip by a soldier or officer.

clue.text: Dining out with social worker, somewhat angry

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the word dining are put out of their order

parts.note: the ant is a social insect and a classic worker

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed at being taken out for dinner with a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' looks like a job in welfare, but crosswords use it for the ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignant describes resentment at unfair treatment, a measured kind of anger.

clue.text: Club porter

parts.note: not a doorman at a gentlemen's club but someone who carries golf clubs round the course

explanation.surface: A doorman or porter working at a members' club.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's bag of clubs and gives advice during a round.

clue.text: A couple of students go to popular comprehensive

parts.note: L is a learner, so two students are two Ls
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Two pupils head off to a well-liked comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'comprehensive' in Britain is a state secondary school taking all abilities, which is the surface sense; the definition is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: All-in means inclusive of everything, as in an all-in price, which is comprehensive.

clue.text: New income below five hundred is diabolical

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece written below comes after the other

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: new suggests the word income is made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh salary under five hundred pounds is a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' places EMONIC, the rearranged INCOME, beneath D in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonic means like a demon, devilish, which is what diabolical means literally.

clue.text: Time to break up when policy matures

definitions.meaning: the close of a school or university session, when pupils break up for the holidays
an insurance policy pays out at the close of its fixed duration

explanation.definitionFit: End of term is both the school holiday start and the expiry date of a fixed-length contract.

clue.text: Outspoken article by G.B. Shaw

parts.note: candid means frank and outspoken
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A frank essay written by George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by G.B. Shaw' defines the answer as a work of his: Candida is an 1894 play by Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Candida is a comedy written by the Irish dramatist George Bernard Shaw.

clue.text: A big hit, poetry that is in fashion

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard, a lam a heavy blow
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A hit poem that is fashionable right now.
explanation.definitionFit: A la mode is borrowed from French for fashionable or up to date.

clue.text: A connection between stories

parts.note: the stories are not tales but floors of a building, joined by flights of steps

explanation.surface: Something that links two narratives together.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase is the set of steps that joins one floor of a building to the next.

clue.text: Adjust rate and things should be different

indicators.note: signals that the letters of rate and things are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A demand to change the rate so that circumstances will change.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten something is to put it right or correct it, a sense of adjust.

clue.text: Vulgar female football supporter rebuffed

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word for a supporter is read backwards

parts.note: a fan supports a team

explanation.surface: A coarse woman who follows football gets turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' turns the whole female football supporter back to front. Naff is British slang for tacky or uncool.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tasteless, cheap or lacking style, much like vulgar.

clue.text: Brief stop for many in a trance

indicators.note: in puts the letter for many inside the word for a trance

parts.note: a coma is a deep unconscious state, like a trance
M is a thousand in Roman numerals, a crossword shorthand for many

explanation.surface: A short break for lots of people who are hypnotised.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma marks a short pause in a sentence, shorter than a full stop.

clue.text: Almost too late to dice

definitions.meaning: to leave very little margin of time
to chop food into small, finely cut cubes

explanation.definitionFit: Cut it fine is an idiom for leaving barely enough time, and literally means chopping finely.

clue.text: Shown to have a deficit and charged

indicators.note: a deficit is a shortfall, so the letter named by the word a goes missing

parts.note: indicated means shown or pointed out

explanation.surface: A firm is revealed to be in the red and is then prosecuted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deficit' takes the A out of INDICATED; the surface makes it sound like a money shortfall.
explanation.definitionFit: To be indicted is to be formally accused of a serious crime in court.

clue.text: These lads may turn out to be immortal

indicators.note: the letters of these and lads may turn out in another arrangement

explanation.surface: These young men may prove to be undying.
explanation.definitionFit: Deathless means never dying, the same as eternal or undying.

clue.text: US visitors to Europe have probably come across it

definitions.text: US visitors to Europe have probably come across it

parts.words: US visitors to Europe have probably come across it
parts.note: come across means travelled over, not encountered, so this is the ocean they cross

explanation.surface: Americans holidaying in Europe have likely encountered this thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic is the ocean lying between North America and Europe.

clue.text: A tug in a storm in the West Indies

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so the letters of a tug in a are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tugboat caught in a Caribbean storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is an island in the Caribbean, part of the Leeward Islands of the West Indies.

clue.text: At the side of a supporter

parts.note: taken as written
a beam is a horizontal timber that holds up a structure

explanation.surface: Someone stands beside a person who backs them.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam is a nautical term for at right angles to a ship's length, alongside it.

clue.text: Broken-hearted, but protected from shock

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of hearted are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone heartbroken yet shielded from emotional shock.
explanation.walkthrough: The shock is electrical, not emotional: an earthed appliance is safe to touch.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthed circuit is connected to the ground so that a fault cannot give an electric shock.

clue.text: Revision of test indicates second thoughts are not always better

definitions.text: indicates second thoughts are not always better

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so the letters of the word test are reordered

explanation.surface: Retaking a test shows that changing your answers is not always wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revision' is also a proofreader's term, fitting the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is a proofreader's mark meaning let the original stand, cancelling a correction.

clue.text: Daughter is accused, but let off

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
taken as written
charged means formally accused of a crime

explanation.surface: A daughter is accused of a crime but released.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a contradiction, accused but freed; the answer is both, as 'discharged' means released by a court.
explanation.definitionFit: To be discharged is to be released from custody or duty, freed without penalty.

clue.text: Shoots game

definitions.meaning: moves suddenly and swiftly, as a fish flits through water
a pub game of throwing small arrows at a board

explanation.definitionFit: Darts are swift movements, and darts is the pub game played with feathered missiles.

clue.text: Features about fifty members of the House of Lords

definitions.text: members of the House of Lords

indicators.note: about means the word for features goes round the numeral

parts.note: ears are features of the face
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Fifty peers are profiled in a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls are a rank of British nobility, historically entitled to sit as peers.

clue.text: Left to resign in chaos, hangs around in hope

indicators.note: chaos throws the letters of resign into disorder

explanation.surface: A politician refuses to quit amid turmoil, waiting for a reprieve.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a politician clinging on; 'Left' is just the letter L, and 'in chaos' is the anagram signal, not the setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay on longer than expected, often reluctant to leave.

clue.text: Chicken and port

definitions.meaning: a breed of domestic fowl originating in Italy
the old English name for Livorno, an Italian seaport

explanation.definitionFit: Leghorn is a breed of laying hen and the traditional English name of the port of Livorno.

clue.text: Pass by the Spanish church feature

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
an apse is the vaulted recess at the east end of a church

explanation.surface: Walking past a feature of a Spanish church.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes by, slipping away unnoticed.

clue.text: Sadie's exchanging confidences

indicators.note: exchanging suggests the letters of Sadie's swap places

parts.note: the name and its possessive ending give all six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Sadie is trading secrets with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are remarks made privately or in confidence, not meant for everyone to hear.
